outlier.evidence: An 8 ('clear accept') against 6, 5 and 4; without it the A mean is 5.0. Two hours at confidence 3, one 'Minor' con (the word 'slot'), no reply to the rebuttal. The summary sells the work as improving out-of-distribution generalisation of RL agents and calls it relevant to the RL community; the paper has no RL or out-of-distribution test.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: Two hours, confidence 3. Four pros and one minor con. Misses the single external baseline, the best-of-runs Table 1 and the absence of any downstream task, and frames the paper as an RL generalisation result it never tests.

checkable_claims.claim: ARI is computed per time step, so nothing measures slot consistency across time.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 269-280 define Encoding and Unroll ARI as mask accuracy against ground truth; no metric tracks identity across frames. The rebuttal says alignment cannot be measured directly 'because the model is unsupervised', but lines 279-280 and Section 4.2 already use ground-truth masks, which give each object's identity.

checkable_claims.claim: No quantitative curve of performance against rollout length.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 1 gives one number per model; Figures 5 and 7 are qualitative.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper does not discuss SCALOR or the other object-centric video models [1-4].
checkable_claims.evidence: None of the four is among the 35 references. The closest cited work is the benchmark of Weis et al. [34].

checkable_claims.claim: The model keeps track of at most M = 12 objects.
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 242: K = 10 MONet slots, M = 12 memory slots. Lines 235-236: each Playroom room holds 10 to 45 objects. Robotics uses M = 8 (Appendix A.1.1).

checkable_claims.claim: Lines 128-129 suggest the memory is fixed during rollout.
checkable_claims.evidence: The unroll equation outputs a memory delta but states no memory update. In B the authors told Reviewer_eFBe the memory updates 'as the equations show'; the equations do not show it.

checkable_claims.claim: Table 1 does not state the unroll length, and footnote 3 is missing.
checkable_claims.evidence: The Table 1 caption gives no length (rebuttal: 15). Footnote mark 3 at line 307 has no text; page 8 carries only footnote 4.

checkable_claims.claim: Only AlignNet is new; the transition model is a simple LSTM.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 133-136 and Appendix A.3: the transition model is a transformer followed by a SlotLSTM, and Figure 10 compares it with other cores. MONet is reused, as the paper says.

checkable_claims.claim: In Figure 5 the model has no input information about the red object it predicts after t = 16.
checkable_claims.evidence: The caption names it the avatar's base, which appears when the agent looks down, so the action input carries it; the Figure 17 caption calls the avatar's appearance a 'predictable consequence of the action space'. The rebuttal instead said the object is visible at t = 0 to 2; those frames show no base.

checkable_claims.claim: No planning or model-based RL experiment, although OP3 has one.
checkable_claims.evidence: The paper has no RL or planning experiment; lines 362-363 leave planning to future work.

checkable_claims.claim: The relation to Ding et al. (2020) is not discussed.

rebuttal.evidence: No A review was edited after posting. Reviewer_NjnN (2021-08-17): 'I'll leave my review as is' and 'I too would like to have seen a comparison to SCALOR'. Reviewer_ayAi, Reviewer_ApBk and Reviewer_sjbW posted nothing after the responses. The responses to ayAi and ApBk are dated 2021-08-25, 15 days after those to NjnN and sjbW; the ApBk one apologises for an earlier mislabelling.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: Nothing visibly moved anyone. The authors dismissed Ding et al. as unpublished, told ApBk a SCALOR baseline 'is not grounds for rejection' and called one of ApBk's statements 'incorrect'. They told ayAi they hoped to share RL results 'in the next few days'; none was posted in A, although B received robot-stacking results on 2021-08-26.

ac.evidence: Ratings split two above and two below threshold. The meta-review takes its reasons from the critics: SCALOR and quantitative evaluation (Reviewer_ApBk, echoed by Reviewer_NjnN) and overall contribution (Reviewer_ayAi). It gives sjbW's 8 no visible weight. Its 'lack of demonstration of object permanence' overstates the reviews: ApBk listed predicted re-appearance after long occlusion as a strength and asked only for recognition at encoding steps, and Figures 6 (t = 30) and 7 (t = 54) show predicted re-appearance qualitatively.

main_reasons_for_decision: Only one external baseline (OP3); no SCALOR or other object-centric video model
Contribution judged small: AlignNet is the only new module
Evaluation measures neither slot consistency over time nor decay with rollout length
AC judged object permanence not demonstrated

outlier.evidence: Ratings run from 5 to 8 around a 6.5 mean; no single score stands apart. The lowest, Reviewer_eFBe's 5, rests on presentation points and a misreading of the task. The highest, Reviewer_sozU's 8, is generous next to its own criticism that the ARI numbers 'did not relate to my visual inspection'.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: Describes the goal as parsing objects 'from third person views' and reads the work as segmentation; the authors had to restate that it is an action-conditioned transition model. Asks where the actions come from, which lines 236-238 state. Opens with a complaint about appendices after the checklist. No reply to the rebuttal.

checkable_claims.claim: Table 1 gives no seed variance for OAT.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 1 caption and checklist 3(c): 'For Table 1 we show the best value for each model' (best of 3 OAT runs and best of 10 OP3 runs, selected on Unroll ARI).

checkable_claims.claim: The abstract's claim that other transition models do not handle persistence and identity satisfactorily ignores SCOFF and NPS.
checkable_claims.evidence: Neither SCOFF nor NPS is cited in the submission; the authors agreed to add them.

checkable_claims.claim: Unroll pixel error includes the background, which dominates it.
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 274 defines it over whole images; lines 277-279 concede the background 'often accounts for most of the pixels'.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper does not define the unroll step precisely.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 119-130 define it: after four observed frames the model feeds back its own predictions with the actions; line 255 restates that it sees only the first four frames.

checkable_claims.claim: The claim that C-SWM will not scale to partially observable scenes has no supporting result.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 214-218 assert it without an experiment; the authors conceded and offered to revise it.

checkable_claims.claim: The work parses objects from third-person views, and the task is segmentation rather than video prediction.
checkable_claims.evidence: Playroom frames are the agent's own view (line 103; Figure 5 caption: the base appears 'when looking down'). The main output is an action-conditioned transition model (Section 2.3).

checkable_claims.claim: Appendix content sits in the main PDF after the references and checklist (pages 12-21).
checkable_claims.evidence: Appendices A-D fill pages 12-21 of the 21-page submission. NeurIPS 2021 allowed technical appendices in the submission PDF, so this is not a violation.

checkable_claims.claim: Lines 128-129 leave unclear what happens to the memory delta in the unroll.
checkable_claims.evidence: The unroll equation outputs a memory delta but states no update; the same gap Reviewer_ApBk found in A.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_gBUs (review edited 2021-08-26): 'I've increased the score to 6', the day the authors posted robot-stacking RL results. Reviewer_V6Rr edited on 2021-09-10 to add 'most of my concerns were resolved'; any rating change is not visible. Reviewer_sozU (2021-08-28) kept 8. Reviewer_Jy59, Reviewer_vmwV and Reviewer_eFBe posted nothing after the responses.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: gBUs tied the score only to a downstream task ('My rating is not effected by how relevant work is mentioned'). The stacking results met that bar although they are thin: OAT against MONet features only, three seeds, one near parity, harder tasks mid-training. gBUs accepted them after the authors said they ran only those seeds. eFBe received clarifications of the task, the actions and the memory update but did not respond.

ac.evidence: Two sentences: 'Reviewers agreed that this is a solid paper that deserves acceptance', plus a request to make the promised changes. Five of six ratings are 6 or above, but eFBe's 5 stood, so 'agreed' overstates. The meta-review names no strength or issue.

Beats OP3 in a 3D partially observable setting
Rebuttal added a downstream robot-stacking result; Reviewer_gBUs rose to 6
Remaining concerns treated as camera-ready fixes

SCALOR and propagation-discovery video models neither cited nor compared (Reviewer_ApBk, Reviewer_NjnN)

shared_issues: Only OP3 as external baseline; other object-centric models not compared (A: ApBk, NjnN; B: Jy59, gBUs)
No downstream RL or planning evaluation (A: ayAi; B: gBUs)
Scalability to many objects and complex scenes (A: ApBk; B: vmwV)
Alignment and re-appearance shown only qualitatively (A: ApBk; B: V6Rr)
Memory update during the unroll unclear at lines 128-129 (A: ApBk; B: eFBe)
MONet description not self-contained (A: ayAi; B: eFBe)
Relation to Ding et al. 2020 (A: NjnN; B: gBUs)
MONet and SlotLSTM reused from prior work (A: ayAi; B: gBUs)
verdict: The committees saw the same paper with the same gaps and weighted them differently; B also saw evidence that A never saw. The gaps are real: OP3 is the only external baseline, there is no downstream or planning task, Table 1 reports best runs without variance, and re-appearance rests on single qualitative examples. In A, Reviewer_ayAi (confidence 5) and Reviewer_ApBk held these gaps against the paper, and the only champion, Reviewer_sjbW (8), wrote a two-hour review with one minor con that the AC gave no visible weight. B drew three satisfied reviewers (Reviewer_sozU 8, Reviewer_vmwV 7, Reviewer_Jy59 7) who accepted the OP3 comparison and the ablation. The authors posted a robot-stacking RL result only in B, and Reviewer_gBUs rose to 6; in A, ayAi was promised RL results 'in the next few days' and none arrived. A's critics got their responses on 2021-08-25, 15 days after the other A responses, including a reply that a missing baseline 'is not grounds for rejection', and neither replied. A's AC then cited a 'lack of demonstration of object permanence', which overstates ApBk's narrower request. No one found an error in a key result; the split comes from reviewer draw, different tolerance for thin baselines, and rebuttal evidence given to one committee only.
